reader.requirement: At --std 85, the two operands of an EVALUATE WHEN ... THROUGH selection object (identifier, literal or arithmetic expression on each side) must be of the same 1985 class (alphabetic, numeric, alphanumeric; edited categories and groups are class alphanumeric, nonnumeric literals alphanumeric, arithmetic expressions numeric), so a pair of different classes is refused and a same-class pair is evaluated as one range.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry range-in-alphabet-2002: the THROUGH range's IN alphabet-name phrase is refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)

reader.edition-search: grep of EvaluateBinder.cs for Edition./DialectBehavior/ConstructRegistry: line 62 (EvaluateObjectsInWhenPhraseOrder, object evaluation order) and line 311 (EvaluateOperandCombinations.IsPermitted, the SR6 pairing) are other rules; ScreenRangeOperands and the IntrinsicArgumentRules class lattice (ClassOf/ClassOf1/ClassOfItem/TableTwoClass/SameClass/CanShareClass) consult no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 1985 has no IN alphabet-name phrase on a THROUGH range (refused at 85, admitted from 2002); the same-class screen is one code for every edition

reader.notes: One reading is open: §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3 (MOVE, elementary move; cite.py OK) says 'The figurative constant SPACE (SPACES) belongs to the category alphabetic', so SPACE THRU <PIC A item> could be argued legal; that sentence is scoped to moves, and the general literal rules make SPACE a nonnumeric literal of category alphanumeric, which is what the compiler applies (the 1985 witness pb5796 also accepts SPACE THRU "Z", consistent only with the alphanumeric reading). Diagnostics name 2023 clauses and the class 'national', which does not exist at 1985 (cosmetic). Same refusals at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-236/runs: r2_neg refuses (COBOL2107) G(group) THRU 9, FUNCTION CHAR (66) THRU 9, 1 THRU SYMB (symbolic-character), LOW-VALUE THRU 9, 1 THRU FUNCTION UPPER-CASE ("A"), A(PIC A) THRU FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (A), FUNCTION ORD ("A") THRU "Z" -- all correct (functions take the class of their category, §1985:IV.4.3.3). r2_pos runs F1..F5 OK and F6 (alphabetic subject, ZERO THRU X, MMM outside 000..BBB) correctly selects OTHER: numeric-function ranges, CHAR THRU symbolic-character, ALL lit THRU ALL lit, ZERO THRU numeric-edited, SYMB THRU QUOTE. The open point is SPACE: the reader rests on 'SPACE is a nonnumeric literal of category alphanumeric', but §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1 defines a nonnumeric literal as one delimited by quotation marks, so its GR3 does not reach SPACE; the ONLY 1985 sentence giving SPACE a category is §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3 ('The figurative constant SPACE (SPACES) belongs to the category alphabetic'). Under that reading SPACE THRU <PIC A item> (refused, reader's c2_space) is legal and SPACE THRU "Z" (accepted, witness pb5796) is two classes. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.13.3 SR4  (║6.13.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR4'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR3  (6.19.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.3  (4.3.3 Concept of Classes of Data)  the text is in the clause'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.2.1  (4.2.2.2.1 Nonnumeric Literals)  the text is in the clause'.
refuter.corrected: CONFORMS for every operand class the 1985 text classes (items, groups, functions, numeric/nonnumeric literals, ZERO, HIGH/LOW-VALUE, QUOTE, symbolic characters, arithmetic expressions); the class of SPACE in a THROUGH range is not stated by 1985 outside MOVE (VI.6.19.4 GR3: alphabetic), so the SPACE arm rests on a reading -- needs an adjudication (and a docs/conformance entry) rather than a CONFORMS on the reader's 'nonnumeric literal' argument.
